title: Refine the video design so it reads as the same app
goal: Video brings a transport, a timeline with lanes, waveforms, channel strips, transition settings and caption lists. That is a lot of new surface arriving at once, into a panel that is already too full. Before any of it is built, work the design through against the rest of the app so it lands as more of Photonz rather than a video editor bolted to the side.
notes:
Asked for by the user on 2026-09-18, immediately after shifting priority to video: "We really need to ensure that we refine the design and ensure things flow with the rest of the app well."

This comes FIRST, before the foundation task, because the panel has just taught everybody what happens otherwise. Three days ago the same user sat down with the component panel and said it was "completely cluttered and hard to read and unpredictable. total mess", and the measuring backed them: 1052 points of sections against a 968 point viewport, with Position and Size never wholly on screen at any window size. Six tasks came out of that. Video adds more surface than components did. Doing the same thing twice would be a choice.

What the panel just learned, and what video must not undo:
- A section is named for the job it does, in words somebody already knows. The app invented Adjustable and Versions and the user could not say what either was for.
- A section that needs a paragraph inside it to explain itself is misnamed; the paragraph is the symptom.
- A grid of number boxes is the laziest answer. One row with a way into the detail, and a Mixed state when the parts differ.
- Things that are set by dragging do not deserve permanent room in the panel: Position and Size left it entirely.
- Panes can be hidden, and there is an automatic mode showing what the selection actually needs.
Every one of those applies to a channel strip, a transition's settings and a caption list as much as it did to a component.

What exists to build on rather than restart: fifteen clickthroughs under docs/design/mocks/pages (video, video-entry-wt, video-cut-wt, video-move-wt, video-zoom-wt, video-freeze-wt, video-title-wt, video-transition-wt, video-transitions, video-captions, video-audio, video-compositing, video-motion, video-speed) plus comp-video, which is the time primitives page and says its own purpose out loud: "Time needs its own primitives, and they are the ones most likely to get re-invented per page because they look like decoration. They are not." The user was explicit that these are ideas rather than specs, so refine them, contradict them where they are wrong, and say where and why.

Also read the pane-load study (work-out-whether-the-right-hand-pane-is-carrying, done) whose page is docs/design/mocks/pages/pane-load.html: it already measured the dock and already recommended a timing strip across the bottom with Motion staying in the panel. That recommendation was made for animation and video inherits the same question, so either follow it or say why video changes the answer.

And the modes work (work-out-whether-the-app-needs-project-types-at) is the other half of this: if a mode is a preset of what is showing, then 'the video surface appears when the document has time' and 'the video mode shows these panes' are the same mechanism described twice. Reconcile them rather than building two.
acceptance: The whole video surface is drawn against the app as it stands, not against an empty window: the same panel, the same layers list, the same tool bar, with time added
Where the new surface goes is settled and shown: what the timeline is, where it lives, what happens to it at a small window and a large one, and what it does when the document has no time

The panel's share is answered specifically, because it is already over budget at 1052 points of sections against a 968 point viewport: say what video adds to it, what it displaces, and what the total comes to

Every new control is checked against the rules the panel just learned: a section is named for what it is for, nothing needs a paragraph inside it to explain itself, and a number that has several parts gets one row and a way in rather than a grid of boxes
The time primitives are drawn once and reused rather than re-invented per page, extending docs/design/mocks/pages/comp-video.html rather than starting beside it
The existing fifteen video pages are reconciled with each other: where two of them answer the same question differently, one answer is chosen and both pages are updated
A person who knows the rest of the app can predict where things are: the audit records a walk-through with somebody who has used Photonz but not this, and what surprised them
It says plainly what it is NOT doing, so the build tasks know their edges
A decision card is opened for the user on anything the design cannot settle on its own
Audit under queue/audits/ with the reconciled pages and the panel budget, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

Put back to p1 on 2026-09-19: a retriage had dropped this to p2, which would have left the video foundation blocked behind every other p1 since it depends on this. The user asked for the design pass specifically ('We really need to ensure that we refine the design and ensure things flow with the rest of the app well') and video is the focus.

Design review 2026-09-19: the shell vocabulary already answers most of this, so start there instead of deriving it again. docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 1 states the rule as 'timeline when time': the timeline dock and transport bar appear only when the document has time, and the bottom dock is item 8 of the regions list with the transport (.transport: volume, skip, play, scrubber with in and out marks, timecodes) above the timeline (.timeline). D8 settles what may sit on the transport row (time controls only, and it gives the table of where everything else goes: a mode to the tool strip, something about the selection next to that selection, something scoped to the timeline to the timeline's own local bar .tlbar). D10 settles that a property list shows what CAN be animated rather than what is. Section 1's responsive rules already say what the transport does at a narrow window. So the finding for this task is not that the vocabulary is missing, it is that the shipped surface does not follow it: a recording today opens its own editor window with its own trim strip, which is the one shape section 1 forbids. Reconcile the fifteen pages against these rules, and where a page and a rule disagree say which one is wrong and change it rather than leaving both.

Manager pass 2026-09-19: there are now PICTURES of the recording window as it actually ships, taken on an unlocked screen this morning from Scripts/playtest/trim-with-pieces-walk.json against HEAD e9d6b163. Two are kept at queue/manager/shots/2026-09-19-video-three-pieces.png (idle, three pieces, one picked) and queue/manager/shots/2026-09-19-video-trim-handles.png (trim mode, handles in). Start the design pass by looking at those rather than at the clickthroughs: four audits in a row say nobody had ever seen this drawn, so this is the first honest picture of the thing being redesigned.

What the pictures say, as input rather than as tasks:

1. There is no shell at all. No tool bar, no layers list, no properties panel, no title text. The window is a player with one floating dark bar across the bottom and a strip of blocks under it. Section 1 of UX-PATTERNS says the timeline dock and transport appear IN the ordinary window when the document has time; what ships is the opposite, so the design is not adding a dock to an existing shell, it is reuniting a window that never had one.

2. The bar teaches two vocabularies. Idle, it is nine unlabelled icon glyphs in a row with no separators and no grouping, and the only words on it are the piece count. In trim mode the icons mostly vanish and three TEXT buttons appear (Reset, Cancel, Done) with two icon buttons, undo and trash, standing beside them. So the same bar is all icons in one state and mostly words in the other, and the transition between them is the answer to 'where did my buttons go'.

3. The bar is flat opaque dark, not a glass surface, so it does not read as the same material as the app's other floating chrome.

4. Accent outline means two different things one keystroke apart. On the strip outside trim mode, an accent outline round a block means THIS is the piece you are holding and the one Delete takes. Inside trim mode, an accent outline round a RANGE means this is the part the handles keep, and everything outside it is what gets thrown away. Same colour, same shape, opposite senses of keep and drop, on the same strip. Whatever the timeline becomes, it needs one meaning for the accent.

5. The strip's loudest signal is progress and its quietest is selection: see the separate task the-piece-you-picked-is-the-faintest-block-on-th for the measured numbers. Worth reading before drawing lanes, because the lane drawing inherits the mistake if nobody names it.

Also for acceptance item 6, the reconciliation: the 2026-09-15 video-cutting audit already recorded where video-cut-wt.html was NOT followed and why, and it is the most useful page in the set for this. It teaches eight steps that need a multi-track timeline, a right hand dock and a tool bar, and its last two steps open a gap and then drag it shut by hand, which the page itself files as wrong. Do not reconcile that page by building it.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE MOCKS, before drawing anything, and it found one thing that changes the whole shape of the work. All fourteen video clickthroughs delete the Layers group from the dock, and video.html says out loud why: 'Layers listed the same seven objects, in the same five groups, in the same order as the timeline - a second rendering of what you had just clicked, so the dock read as having no job. It is gone from this lens.' The complaint is real (163 measured points for a duplicate list) and the conclusion is wrong, three times over: 'this lens' is the language UX-PATTERNS section 1 forbids; two views of one model is what canvas, layers and panel already are; and a video document is full of layers with no time (background, adjustment, matte, component master) which would then have no row anywhere. There is also no escape hatch - PanelSectionVisibility.optionalSections deliberately omits Layers so nothing can hide it. Decided: the pages are wrong, they were corrected, and the rule is now D18.

WHAT THE REVIEW CUT, rather than built. A channel strip (video-audio wants a column of faders: everything in it is either one row in the selection section or a shape over time, so it is a grid of boxes in costume). The Graph as its own panel group (a graph is a picture of time and belongs in the bottom dock; the rule now stands against video.html, which keeps it for now because moving it is building). A caption list on the transport row (D8: time controls only). And a permanent empty Audio track on six pages (a row for a layer that does not exist). SHORTEST VERSION THAT DELIVERS THE SAME VALUE: video needs almost no new chrome at all. The timing strip shipped on 2026-09-15 for animated icons already groups its lanes under the layer they belong to (MotionStripGroup.layerName), already collapses to a rail (motionStripPhase open/row/none), and its own source already says video can take it as it stands. One growth (a layer row draws a bar when it occupies time) and one new panel section (Captions, shaped like Measurements) is the whole of it.

left rough (did not earn its own task, recorded here): (1) video.html's ruler row is still labelled 'Time'. D18 says a ruler is not a row and carries no name; it is built in that page's script rather than its markup and was left. (2) The 92pt label column ellipses 'settings-capture'. That is what the shipping strip does too (MotionStripView.labelWidth = 92) so the mock is honest, but a layer name is the one thing in that column and it gets cut. (3) The Graph group stays in video.html's dock although the design says it moves to the bottom dock; relocating it is building, and it is in the NOT-doing list. (4) Scripts/test.sh had one failure on the first run: IconPreviewRenderTests 'A whole strip of moving previews fits inside one frame of the loop', 56.5ms against a 20ms budget. NOT A REGRESSION and NOT MINE - the gate's own machine yardstick read 10.2ms against its 8.0ms in the same run, i.e. the machine was loaded (by this task's browser and parallel work). Re-run on a quiet machine: 5.8ms with the yardstick at 7.4ms, suite green. Nothing filed; the gate did its job.

Folded into existing tasks rather than filed as new ones: a-document-can-have-time gains the one MotionStrip change (a layer row draws a bar when it has an in and an out) as a log entry and an acceptance item; cut-arrange-and-retime-what-is-on-the-timeline had its acceptance item 1 CORRECTED, because 'the two halves are ordinary layers' means a row per cut and an unusable timeline after five of them - a split adds a PIECE to the same row, which is the word the shipping trim bar already says; appearance-is-below-the-fold-again-because-the-p gains the numbers for what a document with time does to the panel (968 -> 733 with the strip open, 189 over).

THE CARD CAME BACK ANSWERED: 'One window, with a trim mode in it' (option c, the recommended one), resolved 2026-09-20T17:32Z. This run folds the answer into the design rather than blocking again. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE ANSWER BEFORE DRAWING IT, which changed what got drawn: 'Trim is a tool like Crop' is only an answer if Crop is copied exactly, so I read the shipped Crop first (EditorView.cropActionBar). It is Cancel plus a PRIMARY BUTTON NAMED FOR THE VERB on one glass capsule clear of the tool bar, Return commits, Escape cancels, and there is no Done and no Reset beside them. The recording window's Reset/Cancel/Done is therefore a THIRD vocabulary, not the thing being preserved, and the option's 'exactly as they look now' had to be contradicted: keeping those three words would have moved the inconsistency into the main window instead of ending it. So the answer built is Cancel + Trim, with Reset demoted into the settings half of the capsule (a trim is cumulative, unlike a crop, so 'give the whole recording back' is worth keeping).

WHAT LANDED THIS RUN. docs/design/video-surface.md §10 (Trim, answered): what Crop actually does and is copied from; Trim in Crop's slot as a ToolGroup so no slot moves and no new letter is spent (C picks, C again swaps, ⇧C walks, offered only when the document has a duration per D19); handles on the clip's bar with the spare at both ends and its durations; one capsule reading In · Out · kept, Reset, Cancel, Trim, with ⏎ and ⎋; the fast lane kept by what the window OPENS as (a recording that is one clip and has never been edited opens with the clip picked and Trim in hand, so trim-and-send is the same four moves as today, table in §10.3); the two ways to change a clip's length reconciled (§10.4); five awkward corners decided rather than left (§10.5: no clip picked, a layer with no time, clicking another clip mid-session, nothing ever thrown away, pieces stay pieces); what it costs the build in §10.6. UX-PATTERNS D20 generalises it: a focused flow is a tool in the ordinary window and every modal tool ends the same way, never with Done. Mocks: video-shell block 05 draws the whole thing against the real shell, comp-video §08 is the primitive, and the DS gained .clip.trimming, .tspare (video.css) and .cnv .modebar (toolbar.css) so nobody re-invents the session chrome per page.

REVIEW OF THE DRAWN THING, on the real pages in a browser at 1680 wide, both pages screenshotted. What is honest about it: the capsule stacks cleanly over the tool bar and reads as one thing; the clip being trimmed is the loudest thing in the strip and the discarded frames are hatched and quiet, which is the keep/drop confusion in the shipped window finally going the right way round; the panel is the same panel with the same four sections as block 01, so nothing about trim asks the dock for room. What I could not fix and left in the audit's rough list: ic-trim reads as a small rounded rectangle and may not say trim on a real bar; Crop and Trim sharing C is the marquee mechanism applied to two tools far less alike than a box and an ellipse marquee, so it is the first question the audit asks the user; and nobody has drawn the narrow window with the capsule, the transport and the tool bar all stacked (--mb-lift exists for it, unexercised).

FILED, rather than left in this task: the-fourteen-video-pages-still-contradict-the-vi (p2). Fourteen of the fifteen video pages still have no Layers group in the dock, which D18 now forbids, and video-entry-wt still draws a clip's In and Out as a four box grid with a paragraph under it, which §2 and §5 both rule out. The 2026-09-19 pass corrected video.html's caption and renamed rows on fifteen pages but did NOT put the group back, and §7 of the design doc claimed it had; §7 now says what actually happened. Evidence in the task: a one line loop that counts the Layers group on every video page, 0 everywhere but video-shell.

The trim card came back answered ('One window, with a trim mode in it') and the answer is folded in, shipped as 66ac017f. WHAT LANDED: video-surface.md §10, seven sub-sections — what the shipped Crop actually does and is copied from, Trim in Crop's slot as a ToolGroup (the letter belongs to the family, so no slot moves and no new letter is spent), handles on the clip's bar with the spare and its durations at both ends, one capsule reading In · Out · kept then Reset, Cancel, Trim with ⏎ and ⎋, the fast lane kept by what the window OPENS as rather than by a second view, the two ways to change a clip's length reconciled, five awkward corners decided, and what it costs the build. UX-PATTERNS D20 generalises it.
